clue.text: Space gone over in open land

indicators.note: gone over suggests passing back across, so the synonym is read backwards

parts.note: space means room, as in room to move

explanation.surface: Somebody notes that a stretch of empty space has been crossed on wild open country.
explanation.definitionFit: A moor is a stretch of uncultivated upland, open land covered with heather or grass.

clue.text: Maiden in charge of costumes, hazards to health?

parts.note: M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over
robes are costumes or garments

explanation.surface: A young woman runs the wardrobe department, whose outfits are somehow a danger to everyone's wellbeing.
explanation.definitionFit: Germs and bacteria are tiny organisms that can cause disease, hence health hazards; the question mark flags the loose description.

clue.text: Sort out drinks — conference speakers may need them

indicators.note: sort out means arrange, so the letters of sort are put into a new order

parts.note: rums are tots of spirit, drinks

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to organise the refreshments, since speakers at a conference will need something to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns SORT into ROST; the surface makes 'drinks' seem to be what the speakers need.
explanation.definitionFit: Speakers at a conference stand at raised platforms or lecterns to address the audience.

clue.text: Footballers given special experience, we hear, in town's hidden part?

parts.note: backs are defensive players in a football team

indicators.note: signals that the word for a special experience is taken by its sound rather than spelling

parts.note: a treat is a special, enjoyable experience

explanation.surface: A football team is given a special outing, apparently in some secret corner of the town.
explanation.definitionFit: A side street away from the main roads is an out-of-the-way, little-seen part of a town.

clue.text: Busy person entertaining a guest, surprisingly gracious act

indicators.note: entertaining means holding within, as a host holds a guest

parts.note: a busy bee is a proverbially industrious person

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests the letters of guest turn up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A hard-working host takes in a visitor, which turns out to be a remarkably generous gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Busy person' is the crossword's bee, and the answer is the French phrase, also a famous novel title; 'surprisingly' rearranges the guest's letters as UGEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Beau geste is a French phrase borrowed into English for a noble, magnanimous gesture.

clue.text: Keeps up unrealistic plans

parts.note: keeps are the strongholds of fortresses, so castles
up, as something airborne, means in the air

explanation.surface: Someone stubbornly maintains plans that have no grounding in reality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeps' looks like a verb but is the noun, fortress towers.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes daydreams and schemes with no chance of coming true.

clue.text: The termination of concert pianist's tours?

indicators.note: the termination of a word is its final letter, taken here from concert

parts.note: Maurice Ravel, the French composer, was also a pianist; with the possessive, Ravel's

explanation.surface: A query whether the end of a concert pianist's tours has come.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'tours' as a noun; as the definition it is the verb, goes on journeys.
explanation.definitionFit: To tour is to journey from place to place, the same as making journeys.

clue.text: Cede, alas, when beaten in mounted attack

indicators.note: beaten suggests the letters are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: A defeated side gives way, sadly, as cavalry charge at them.
explanation.definitionFit: An escalade is an assault on fortifications by scaling the walls with ladders, so an attack that climbs up.

clue.text: Restricted around end of career and ready to retire

indicators.note: around means the restricting word goes about the letter that follows

parts.note: tied means restricted or bound

indicators.note: end of a word is its final letter, taken from career

explanation.surface: Someone whose working life has been confined is approaching its close and ready to stop work.
explanation.definitionFit: Being weary and in need of rest means being ready to go to bed, to retire for the night.

clue.text: Plant enabling agents to capture idiot

indicators.note: to capture means to hold within, so the agents enclose the fool

parts.note: the CIA is the American intelligence agency, staffed by agents
an ass is a fool or idiot

explanation.surface: A spy plant has let secret agents seize a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' suggests a mole or informer; it is the botanical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassia is a genus of tropical shrubs and trees, one source of senna and cinnamon-like bark.

clue.text: Mark crosses square in police vehicle

indicators.note: crosses means goes across and around, so the mark encloses the square

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin
a quad is a quadrangle, a square courtyard

explanation.surface: A man called Mark walks across a town square in a police car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name; it is a blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: A patrol car used by police officers on duty is a standard term in crime drama.

clue.text: Nothing given to one naughty girl — one may get into bed

parts.note: O, the zero shape, means nothing
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: naughty suggests the letters of girl misbehave into a new order

explanation.surface: A racy picture of a naughty girl climbing into bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given to' joins the pieces; 'naughty' turns GIRL into LRIG. The bed is the seabed.
explanation.definitionFit: Offshore drilling platforms bore into the seabed to extract petroleum.

clue.text: Boy hugging beautiful woman is given name

indicators.note: hugging means wrapping around, so the boy encloses the woman

parts.note: a lad is a boy
a belle is a beautiful woman

explanation.surface: A young man embraces a lovely woman, who is then given a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tagged or described with a word or title has been given a name.

clue.text: People doing the wrong thing in terrible ruse when lass comes round

indicators.note: comes round means encircles the shuffled letters

parts.note: a miss is a girl or lass

indicators.note: terrible suggests the letters of ruse are badly mangled

explanation.surface: Wrongdoers are caught in a dreadful trick when a young woman pays a visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' and 'in' are only links; the surface's ruse is a trick, but here it is just the letters that 'terrible' rearranges into USER.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who abuse or wrongly apply something are using it improperly, doing the wrong thing with it.

clue.text: Rail-user's excited — leaves the big city behind?

indicators.note: excited suggests the letters are agitated into a new order

explanation.surface: A train passenger is thrilled as the train pulls out of the metropolis.
explanation.definitionFit: To become countrified is to adopt country ways, abandoning urban life; the question mark flags the loose reading.

clue.text: Boys? Bright types from what we hear

indicators.note: signals that the word for bright types is taken by its sound

parts.note: suns are bright bodies; the stars of the sky

explanation.surface: Are boys clever, judging by the reports?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bright types' suggests clever people; they are stars.
explanation.definitionFit: A family's male children are its boys.

clue.text: Notice cancelling barbecue meal? A tricky situation

definitions.meaning: read literally, a sign that outdoor eating is not happening
the idiom for something difficult, not easy at all

explanation.surface: A sign calls off the barbecue, leaving the hosts in an awkward position.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means no easy task, a difficult business; literally a sign banning outdoor eating.

clue.text: It's bound to be quiet at far side of meadow

indicators.note: at far side of means the quiet letter goes after the meadow

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for a meadow
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet

explanation.surface: Something is sure to be silent at the far end of a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' looks like 'certain' (bound to be); it is a jump.
explanation.definitionFit: A bound is a jump, so a jump is a bound.

clue.text: Writing that keeps doing the rounds over a period of time

definitions.meaning: handwriting done by pen, not typed or in shorthand

definitions.text: that keeps doing the rounds over a period of time
definitions.meaning: the minute hand of a clock, going round once each hour

explanation.surface: Some piece of writing keeps circulating for a long while.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary handwriting with words written out in full; also a clock's minute pointer, which circles the face hourly.

clue.text: Keep quiet about wait

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet
re is Latin for about, concerning
to wait at table is to serve

explanation.surface: An instruction to stay silent about having to wait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep quiet' reads as one phrase, but 'Keep' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something safe or unchanged is to save it from decay.

clue.text: Real don, exceptional old genius in many fields

indicators.note: exceptional suggests the letters are out of the ordinary order

explanation.surface: A true university fellow, an outstanding elder polymath.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo da Vinci was painter, engineer, anatomist and inventor, the archetypal Renaissance polymath.

clue.text: Fish in lake in the morning to get something caught?

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake
AM is ante meridiem, in the morning
prey is what a hunter catches

explanation.surface: An angler fishes in a lake at dawn hoping to land something.
explanation.definitionFit: The lamprey is an eel-like jawless fish that sucks on other fish.

clue.text: Somewhat OTT adult sank teeth into chum wickedly!

parts.note: A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult
bit is the past tense of bite, sank teeth into

indicators.note: wickedly suggests the letters of chum are cruelly twisted

explanation.surface: A grown-up bit a friend, which seems rather over the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wickedly' turns CHUM into MUCH. OTT means over the top.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means rather excessive, going too far: somewhat over the top.

clue.text: Storyteller producing a work about French art

indicators.note: about means going around the French word

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
es is French for 'art', as in tu es (you are)

explanation.surface: A writer produces a piece about painting in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'art' is the old second-person form of 'are', in French es; 'art' looks like painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek teller of fables such as the tortoise and the hare.

clue.text: Conspicuous people given insults heading off

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: slights are insults or snubs

explanation.surface: Prominent figures are snubbed and then storm off.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the S at the front of SLIGHTS leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Leading lights are prominent, notable figures, as in luminaries.

clue.text: Foreign lass in Home Counties, no educated girl

parts.note: SE, the south-east of England, is where the Home Counties around London lie
Rita is the heroine of Educating Rita, Willy Russell's play and film

explanation.surface: A foreign young woman living near London lacks a school-educated companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Señorita is the Spanish word for an unmarried young woman, a lass abroad.

clue.text: Quiet state for young man

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
aver means state or assert

explanation.surface: A demand for silence aimed at a youth.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaver is an old informal word for a lad or youngster, as in young shaver.

clue.text: Camp's in trouble with herd, ending with frisky elephants?

indicators.note: in trouble suggests the letters are thrown into disarray
ending means the last letter of frisky

explanation.surface: A camp is under threat from a lively herd of elephants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ending' takes Y from 'frisky' into the anagram of CAMPS and HERD.
explanation.definitionFit: Thick-skinned large mammals such as elephants and rhinos; the question mark notes elephants are an example.

clue.text: Pantomime character made to look silly

indicators.note: made to look silly suggests the letters are rearranged foolishly

explanation.surface: A pantomime performer is made to look ridiculous.
explanation.definitionFit: The pantomime dame is a stock comic role in British Christmas pantomime, an older woman played by a man.
